one_line_summary: Design rule: use moisture-tolerant sorbents for CO2 capture under humid conditions

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use moisture-tolerant sorbents for CO2 capture under humid conditions → sorbents remain stable while capturing CO2 under humid conditions

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] tune pore size and framework functionality in pillar-layered Zn-triazolate-dicarboxylate frameworks → associated with high CO2/CH4 and C2 hydrocarbons/CH4 selectivity

notable_quotes: Changing the dicarboxylate linker from Fuma to BDC markedly lowers the reported separation metrics, indicating linker choice only partially preserves performance.
Zn2(TRZ)2(Fuma) shows much stronger 50/50 CO2 capture performance than Zn2(TRZ)2(BDC), with values of 3.92 vs 1.52 under the reported test conditions.
Using mixed-linker MOFs is proposed as a strategy for carbon and hydrocarbon capture under moist conditions.
